props.title: When Harry Met Sally
props.initialSlug: Two friends battle love over twelve years of "just friends"

sections.content: When Harry Met Sally revolutionized romantic comedies by grounding the genre in razor-sharp observations about male-female friendships. Rob Reiner's direction and Nora Ephron's screenplay created a blueprint that countless films tried to replicate - the slow-burn friendship-to-romance arc, the witty banter, the split-screen conversations, and that legendary Katz's Deli scene. The film's influence echoes through Sleepless in Seattle (1993), You've Got Mail (1998), and modern hits like 500 Days of Summer (2009). What sets it apart is the authentic chemistry between Billy Crystal and Meg Ryan, plus the innovative use of documentary-style elderly couple interviews that add depth to the film's exploration of lasting love.

sections.content: The film's New York setting becomes a character itself, following the tradition of Manhattan (1979) and predating Serendipity (2001). Cinematographer Barry Sonnenfeld captures autumn-draped Central Park, cozy bookstores, and Washington Square in ways that make the city feel simultaneously grand and intimate. This visual approach influenced countless rom-coms, from 13 Going on 30 (2004) to Nick and Norah's Infinite Playlist (2008), establishing New York as the de facto setting for sophisticated romantic comedies. SUBHEAD: The Evolution of Modern Romance in Cinema

What makes When Harry Met Sally particularly relevant is how it tackles the complexities of modern relationships. Unlike earlier romantic comedies that relied on meet-cutes and misunderstandings, this film explores the genuine evolution of friendship and attraction. This sophisticated approach influenced films like Friends with Benefits (2011) and No Strings Attached (2011), which similarly examine whether platonic relationships between men and women can exist. The film's honest dialogue about sex and relationships paved the way for frank discussions in later works like Bridget Jones's Diary (2001) and Knocked Up (2007).
